title: Textonomy: A TnT-LLM-Based Approach for Interpretable Topic Modeling at Scale
venue: Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Natural Language and Speech Processing (ICNLSP 2026)
problem: Interpretability-scalability-accessibility trilemma: LDA/BERTopic need interpretation; per-document LLM methods such as TopicGPT are slow, costly and often closed-source.
architecture: Implementation of TnT-LLM: Phase 1 an LLM summarises a small document sample and iteratively builds a taxonomy guided by the analyst's goal; Phase 2 an LLM pseudo-labels a training subset and a lightweight classifier is trained for large-scale assignment.
llm_or_encoder: o3-mini (taxonomy) and GPT-4o-mini (summaries, labels); open-source variant Mistral-Large-Instruct-2411
metrics: P1 (harmonic mean of purity and inverse purity)
key_results: Wiki: Textonomy average P1 0.73, ARI 0.68, NMI 0.66 vs TopicGPT 0.73/0.58/0.71 and BERTopic 0.46/0.12/0.37.
Bills: open-source variant best run P1 0.56, ARI 0.39 vs TopicGPT 0.57/0.42 (default); proprietary average 0.47/0.31.
About 6.8 minutes and about $0.93 per Wiki run vs an estimated 450 minutes and $155 for TopicGPT.
strengths: Cuts LLM cost by over 99% while keeping alignment close to TopicGPT.
Stable across reruns, prompts and training samples (ARI about 0.71-0.79 against the default run); open-source variant provided.

limitations.text: Possible memorisation of Wikipedia by LLMs; alignment metrics assume one topic per document and depend on k, which differed across methods without a matched-k analysis.
Relies on LLM APIs (cost, model changes, non-determinism).
On Bills, TopicGPT remains better on all three alignment metrics.

notes: Uses the Wiki and Bills versions prepared by Pham et al. (TopicGPT).
